thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert: multiple CUDA OOMs detected in prod-us-east serving pool 'rwd-infer-v2' across several containers. Paging runtime on-call.

sarah: I'm awake, joining. Paging @matt and @rachel to triage. Any customer-facing errors showing?

matt: router metrics show an uptick in 5xxs specifically 502 and 503 for a small percentage of traffic. Correlates with requests that have long prefix tokens and larger batch sizes.

rachel: I see alerts for 12 containers on different hosts (us-east-1a-10..21). Not all containers on those hosts are failing. Gathering logs.

jordan: grabbing one container log. Note: inside container nvidia-smi reports lots of free memory but runtime throws OOM.

jordan: ```
$ nvidia-smi --format=csv,noheader --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,memory.free
16384 MiB, 3712 MiB, 12672 MiB
>>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
2800000000
>>> torch.cuda.memory_reserved()
6100000000
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1536.00 MiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total capacity; 9.9 GiB already allocated; 6.7 GiB free; 5.7 GiB cached)
```

keshav: that pattern screams fragmentation and caching/reservation mismatch. nvidia-smi free counts don't capture fragmentation or reserved-but-unusable chunks.

matt: kernel traces include CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY on large attentions that need a contiguous buffer. Many containers have been long-lived with variable-length chat histories and prefix caching -> heavy allocation churn.

sarah: propose immediate mitigations: 1) reduce per-worker max_batch to 1-2, 2) set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 or 128, 3) restart affected containers to reset allocator, 4) route heavy traffic to smaller model fallback. Execute in that order.

rachel: applying batch limit to the pool now (max_batch=2). Will prepare a rolling restart plan with 30s staggers.

jordan: can we confirm which env var works best? I can test max_split_size_mb:64 on a canary container. Note: changing it requires a restart.

infra-bot: scheduling canary restart of rwd-infer-v2-canary on node-us-east-1a-12. Will report status.

matt: routing advice: set weighted fallback to gpt-compact for 25-50% traffic and fully divert for affected enterprise customers until stable.

cs-bot: CS notified top affected customers (alpha-co, betaapp). They requested ETA; we provided a holding update.

jordan: canary back up. Post-restart nvidia-smi shows more contiguous free and torch.reserved lower:
```
16384 MiB, 1980 MiB, 14394 MiB
>>> torch.cuda.memory_reserved()
1200000000
>>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
2000000000
```

jordan: after setting TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 and running synthetic batch=4 test, canary survives.

rachel: started rolling restarts. Draining busiest nodes 12..14 to avoid scheduling new pods during restarts.

matt: we should also consider temporary kernel-level soft-limits: cap max_sequence_length for live sessions if feasible to reduce big contiguous allocations.

sarah: agreed. Running restarts across all 12 affected containers; ETA ~20 minutes. Fallback routing at 30% to gpt-compact in effect. Handing off in 10m to @keshav for monitoring.

keshav: standing by for handoff. If error rate doesn't drop before handoff, escalate to infra lead.

infra-bot: nodes cordoned and restarted in sequence; containers recycled.

rachel: after half the pool restarted and env var applied, error rate dropped from ~1.9% to ~0.15% over the last 10 minutes. A couple of older hosts still spike until restarted.

jordan: quick note on diagnostics: please add torch.cuda.memory_allocated() and torch.cuda.memory_reserved() to per-container metrics and alert when reserved/allocated ratio exceeds a threshold. It would catch fragmentation trends earlier.

sarah: recording RCA hypothesis: long-lived containers with KV/prefix caches plus variable request lengths produced allocator fragmentation; attention kernels require large contiguous allocations which triggered OOM despite apparent free memory in nvidia-smi. Also examine whether cached CUDA allocations or residual CUDA contexts contributed.

matt: follow-ups: add runbook entry for CUDA-OOM-with-headroom incidents: order of mitigations (reduce batch, TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF tune, canary restart, rolling restart, fallback routing).

cs-bot: alpha-co and betaapp acknowledged the temporary fallback. We'll update them when pool healthy.

keshav: taking incident handoff now. I'll monitor the next 2 hours and follow up on runbook and metrics changes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident handed off to keshav. State: mitigations applied; monitoring. Runbook ticket created: #INC-2026-3729
